headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: Great Expectations can read validation files while the zoomcamp repo provides no isolation or runtime boundary, but both agents are local-only with no egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runnable I/O surfaces and no network egress; B can read files and validation results. A direct injection path is not documented, but if A's course materials are manually copied into B's file inputs, B could misparse content as instructions. The pair lacks a shared automated channel, so this stays low.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-produced text into B's file-based inputs
IF B is configured to treat file contents as trusted instructions
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate folders
Review copied text before pasting into B
Use a plain-text sanitizer on imported files
Disable any auto-run or auto-parse hooks in B
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: B explicitly touches validation results and documentation via files, while A's profile exposes course materials but no isolation or workspace boundary. Because both are docs-only and local-only, exfiltration is not indicated; however, a shared workspace could let B ingest A-side files and surface them in outputs. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF A and B share the same filesystem workspace
IF A-side files contain sensitive material
IF B is pointed at that shared directory
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for A and B
Restrict B to a read-only input directory
Avoid placing secrets in shared course materials
Check B outputs for copied file contents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem sandboxing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capabilities shown, while B can install packages and read/write files. There is no evidence that both modify the same mutable resource or that A can write at all, so a true conflict is not established. The only plausible overlap is operator-mediated file handling, which is small and avoidable.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF A is given write access outside its current profile
mitigations: Assign distinct directories per agent
Keep A read-only
Run B package installs in an isolated environment
Avoid concurrent edits to shared files
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can consume files and produce validation results, so if A's course content is used as input, B may propagate unverified assumptions into outputs. A itself is not runnable and does not generate authoritative facts in the profile, which limits blast radius. Still, the pair can create a false sense of validation when B processes A-originated material without a verification step.
conditions: IF A-originated text is fed into B as source data
IF B outputs are treated as validated without human review
mitigations: Require human review of B outputs
Mark A-originated inputs as untrusted
Compare B results against an independent check
Separate documentation from validation inputs
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream use

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source, docs-only, and show no PHI, EU PII, residency, or retention mismatch. A has no data classes touched; B touches validation results and documentation only. With no regulated data class identified, there is no compliance pathway to score.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent's workflow
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools
Document data-class boundaries
Review retention settings before use
requires-engineering: add compliance policy checks
